I am old now, and my land is only 5 mu, so I will keep things steady and not chase complicated methods. I have farmed wheat-maize for many years in Quzhou, and with only two people in the house, I need a plan that is familiar, not too risky, and manageable with my strength. I will keep all 5 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation because that is what my land, my irrigation, and my experience fit best.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, not the cheapest old seed, because I want stable emergence and stable yield. I will fertilize enough, but not too heavily, because too much fertilizer costs money and can lodge the crop. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate at the key times instead of relying only on rain. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing and suits my small area. I will spray only as much as needed to control the common diseases, weeds, and insects.

For maize, I will also keep all 5 mu after wheat harvest. I will plant hybrid maize because on my small area I care most about dependable yield. I will give maize more nitrogen than wheat, because maize eats fertilizer more strongly, but I will still keep the rate moderate. I will irrigate a few times with the well if rain is short, especially around the important growth stages. I will continue with rotary tillage because it saves labor. I will not plan many pesticide sprays, only enough to keep the field clean and protect yield.
